The action's inputs Input Required Default Meaning target yes Target id, as listed in targets.json report yes Path of objdiff's report.json for this target targets no config/targets.json The producer's targets file site no config/site.json The producer's presentation file tools no empty Measured-with tools, one name=version per line; shown on the page as provenance measured-at no now UTC time of the measurement, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ code-sections no .init,.text Comma-separated code section names; every other section counts as data unit-prefix no main/ Prefix stripped from objdiff unit names for display credits no config/<target>/credits.tsv when it exists Credit overrides; read only when contributors are on github-token no the workflow token Reads the merged PR and the credited people when contributors are on; the target job grants pull-requests: read data-repository no mitsevox/decomp-data owner/name of the data repository app-client-id yes Client id of the GitHub App installed on the data repository app-private-key yes Private key of that GitHub App The starter workflow passes target , report , tools , measured-at , app-client-id and app-private-key and leaves the rest at their defaults. The tools lines come from tools/measuring_tools.py --verify : build-environment=<image digest> , then one line per tag it reads from configure.py ( dtk=v1.8.3 , objdiff=v3.6.1 in the starter) or per entry of its pin files; the versions are the repository's pins, and --verify has just confirmed each tool its VERIFY parameter names against the image ( CI ). What the action does Splits data-repository into owner and name. Mints the token with actions/create-github-app-token (pinned to its v3.3.0 commit), with owner , repositories: <name> and permission-contents: write . Runs python3 "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/publish.py" publish --target ... --report ... --targets ... --site ... --tools ... --measured-at ... --code-sections ... --unit-prefix ... --data-repository ... with the token in the environment variable DATA_TOKEN . publish.py is standard-library Python and runs inside the build image, which is why the image needs python3 and git . publish.py publish then: Reads the report, targets.json and site.json , and builds game.json , latest.json and map.json in memory. repository comes from GITHUB_REPOSITORY ; the measured revision, its commit time and subject come from git log -1 on the checkout; source.url and source.runUrl are built from GITHUB_SERVER_URL , GITHUB_REPOSITORY and GITHUB_RUN_ID . Clones the data repository at depth 1 using the token (sent as an HTTP header through the environment, never on a command line) and configures the committer as <slug> publisher <publisher@users.noreply.github.com> . Up to five times: resets to the newest tip of the default branch, writes the target's files, runs the full tree check, commits as <slug> <target>: <7-char sha>, <n>% code linked with the run URL as the body, and pushes. A lost race (another target or game pushed in between) is retried from the new tip; the write is idempotent, so a retry re-applies the same measurement. Prints published <slug>/<target> <sha> , or <slug>/<target> <sha> already published when nothing changed. Writing the target's files follows two rules that make re-runs and out-of-order runs safe: the first measurement of a revision wins (re-running the workflow for the same commit changes nothing), and latest.json and map.json only move forward by commit time (a slow run of an older commit never replaces a newer one). The history row for the revision is appended either way, and latest.json 's digests follow the files on every write. The exact file formats are in Data contract . Because the action runs at @main in every producer, a change to it is live for every producer's next main run the moment it merges. A change that spans the site, the data repository and a producer merges in that order: the site first (the action and the checker), then the data repository (a correction or a migration of the data), then the producer; the site's CI checks the live data with the new checker before the site change merges ( Data contract ). Correcting published data A publish never rewrites a published revision: re-running the workflow for the same commit keeps what was published, and a new commit publishes a new measurement beside it. A published file that is wrong is corrected in the data repository, by hand, and nowhere else: Clone the data repository and make the smallest edit that makes the file right (the two data-fuzzy values of one unit in map.json , say). Never change a measurement in history.json unless that row itself was wrong, and never remove a row. From the site repository's checkout, python3 .github/actions/publish/publish.py reseal <clone> : it rewrites digests in each latest.json whose files changed and prints them, then runs the whole tree check. Then python3 tools/check_data_tree.py <clone> , the page's own validator, which the publisher's checker does not replace: the one correction made so far was refused by the page's rules alone. Merge only when both readers accept. Without the reseal, publish.py check and the site's live-data check refuse the tree ( map.json: digest differs from latest.json ). Open a pull request against the data repository that states the reason, merge it; the Deploy workflow publishes it. The data repository has no CI of its own, so run python3 tools/check_data_tree.py once more on a fresh clone of the merged branch (a checkout that converts line endings would have digested other bytes than Git commits); the site's daily Live data job repeats that check. The page fetches map.json , history.json and contributors.json by their digest, so the corrected file has a new URL and no browser shows the old copy; latest.json itself is always revalidated. The measurement's revision and time stay what they were: a correction changes a file, not the measurement's identity. (The page also refetches a cached map once past the cache when it fails validation, but a correction must not depend on that.) Credits Credits are optional per repository: "contributors": true in config/site.json switches them on, and nothing changes while it is false or absent. With them on, each main build also writes contributors.json : Who. The PR whose merge made the measured revision ( GET /repos/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls ). Its body's Credits: @login, @login line names the people; without the line its author is credited. An agent working under the owner's login is the author of its PRs, so its work is credited to the owner unless the PR's Credits: line names someone else. A revision that no PR merged credits nobody and fails the publish. What. A function is credited to the people of the earliest measured main build in which it was exact. Newly exact functions take this build's people; functions already credited keep theirs; a function that is no longer exact moves to retired with its credit, and gets that credit back when it returns. An older commit whose run finishes late moves a credit earlier when it was exact first, and adds or retires nothing, because latest.json decides what is exact now. Switching on. The first build with credits on credits every function already exact to the repository owner. Overrides. config/<target>/credits.tsv (address, comma-separated logins, reason; # comments allowed) credits the listed functions to those people whatever the merges say: for batches that carry other people's work, imports and corrections. It is reviewed like any other record. The pull request side runs before merge: the plan job's Check the credits step ( tools/credits.py ) does nothing while credits are off, and otherwise checks the Credits: line and every credits.tsv and confirms that each login exists, so a bad credit fails the PR and never the publish on main . Everything written is checked before the push by the same code as publish.py check , so a bad conversion fails the job instead of landing in the data repository. The target must be active in targets.json ; publishing a planned target stops with Target <id> is not an active target of <slug> . Verifying a publish In the Validate <target id> job log, the Publish to the site step prints published game/GAME01-rev0 <sha> . The data repository has a new commit by game publisher ; its Deploy workflow runs (about a minute). https://mitsevox.github.io/decomp-data/data/game/GAME01-rev0/latest.json shows the new source.revision . https://mitsevox.github.io/games/game/ shows the new numbers. The page revalidates latest.json on every view and fetches the other files by digest, so a reload is enough. Running the conversion locally The action's script runs anywhere with Python 3 and Git. From the producer checkout, after a local build: git clone https://github.com/mitsevox/mitsevox.github.io site python3 site/.github/actions/publish/publish.py publish --target GAME01-rev0 \ --report build/GAME01-rev0/report.json --repository owner/game \ --tools "$(python3 tools/measuring_tools.py)" --dry-run --no-credits --output /tmp/tree python3 site/.github/actions/publish/publish.py check /tmp/tree --dry-run writes the files into --output (or a temporary directory) and pushes nothing; --no-credits leaves the credits out, which otherwise need the merged pull request on GitHub; check validates a whole tree. --repository is required outside Actions because GITHUB_REPOSITORY is unset; source.runUrl is null locally. This is the same conversion the Check the report step runs on every pull request ( CI ), and the only way to inspect the generated files. Both write into an empty tree: whether the measurement merges with the published history (one row per revision, in order) is checked by the publish itself. Before the first push to main The App is installed on the data repository with Contents read and write. The producer has the variable and the publish environment with its branch policy and secret, and validate.yml names them. config/targets.json and config/site.json validate ( python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' and a dry run). A pull request has passed Validate targets , whose Check the report step converted this target's report. Then merge. The first publish creates data/<slug>/ and adds the slug to index.json ; no one edits the data repository for a new game except to add cover art ( The site ).

title: Repository settings
summary: Branch rules, merge method, Actions permissions, credentials and presentation: the standard, the script that applies it and the monthly check.
text: Repository settings Branch rules, merge method, Actions permissions, credentials, security features and presentation, applied by a script and re-checked monthly. Settings are part of the standard because they are what makes the rest enforceable: a required check means nothing on a branch that accepts direct pushes, and a read-only default token is what keeps a workflow from approving its own PR. Three kinds of repository are in scope: the public source repository, the private build repository and the site. The data repository receives pushes from the publishing App and has its own settings. The standard Setting Source repository Build repository Site repository Default branch main main main Ruleset main require a pull request; required check Validate targets ; block force pushes and deletion; no bypass actors none: rulesets on a private repository need a paid plan, and only the owner can push there require a pull request; required check Test ; block force pushes and deletion; no bypass actors Ruleset merges one update rule; its only bypass actor is the Repository admin role with bypass mode "pull requests only" none none Merge method squash only squash only squash only Auto-delete head branches on on on Allowed actions GitHub-owned, plus mitsevox/mitsevox.github.io/.github/actions/* GitHub-owned only GitHub-owned only Default GITHUB_TOKEN read-only; workflows declare their own permissions read-only read-only Actions may approve pull requests off off off Fork pull request approval required for all outside collaborators (the fork guard in validate.yml is the second line) not applicable required for all outside collaborators Artifact and log retention 30 days 30 days 30 days Variable and secret the repository variable DATA_APP_CLIENT_ID ; no repository secret none; GITHUB_TOKEN publishes the image SETTINGS_READ_TOKEN for the monthly check Environments publish : deployment branches main only (no tag rule), the secret DATA_APP_PRIVATE_KEY , nothing else; validate : every branch, no secrets none none Package not applicable private; Manage Actions access grants the source repository Read not applicable Secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot alerts, private vulnerability reporting on on where the plan allows on Dependabot version updates off; pinned actions are bumped by hand twice a year off off Issues on off on (the drift issue) Wiki, Projects, Discussions off off off Description, homepage, topics <Title> (<console>, <year>) decompilation ; https://mitsevox.github.io/games/<slug>/ ; decompilation , <platform> , <slug> Private build environment for <owner>/<game> ; none; none the repository's own Two rulesets protect main in a source repository. main makes every change a pull request that passed Validate targets . merges decides who may merge: contributors hold write access, because CI refuses a fork's pull request (a fork's build would reach the private image), and write access alone would let a contributor merge a pull request that passed CI. The update rule restricts updates of main to the ruleset's bypass actors, and the only one is the Repository admin role in "pull requests only" mode: a writer pushes branches and opens pull requests but cannot merge, the owner merges through a pull request, and nobody, the owner included, pushes to main directly. GitHub shows the rule as "Restrict updates" and the bypass as "Repository admin, Pull requests only". Each ruleset --check reads is the one with the standard's name, or else the one of that shape that targets the default branch under another name ( merges is the ruleset whose only rule is update ), never the same ruleset for both; --apply then renames it rather than adding a second one. An update rule inside main is drift: with no bypass actor there, nobody could merge. It also compares the pull request rule's merge methods and stale-approval dismissal, and the up-to-date requirement, which stays off: main rebuilds and verifies after every merge. A single setting may differ for one repository (a merge method, say) when its process needs it; that is a row in the per-repository overrides of the configuration file, never a change to the table. The script The standard is data: config/repo-standard.json in the site repository holds the table keyed by kind, a repositories block that names each repository with the values its description, homepage and topics are built from, and the overrides. tools/repo_settings.py reads it and talks to the GitHub REST API; standard-library Python, idempotent. export GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" python3 tools/repo_settings.py --repo owner/game --check python3 tools/repo_settings.py --repo owner/game --apply python3 tools/repo_settings.py --all --check --check prints one line per setting that differs ( expected ..., found ... ) and exits 1 when anything does. A setting the token cannot read counts as drift, so a check never passes blind. --apply sets, in this order, the repository fields and features, the merge settings, the Actions permissions and allowlist, the default token permissions, fork approval, retention, the main and merges rulesets (each created or updated by name), the environments with their deployment branch policies, and the security features, then re-reads everything and prints what remains. A repository that is not listed in the configuration is checked against its kind alone ( --kind source or --kind build ), and its description, homepage and topics are its own. What the script cannot set, and prints as hand steps: the variable (Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions) and the environment secret (Settings, Environments, publish ), and deleting any others; a DATA_APP_PRIVATE_KEY repository secret goes only at its step of the move order below; the private package's Manage Actions access grant to the source repository; the GitHub App that writes the data repository ( Publishing ); removing a .github/dependabot.yml if one exists. The owner runs --apply with their own token once per repository after it adopts the standard, and after any deliberate change to the table. Keeping it true Two readers keep the settings from drifting back: The scaffold check , in every repository's Tool tests job ( CI ), reads what the default GITHUB_TOKEN can see without any extra permission: the description, homepage, topics, features, merge settings and the rules that apply to main ( GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/main , the union of both rulesets, so a missing update rule shows there). It warns on each difference next to its other findings. It can read neither Actions permissions nor secrets, and it never writes. The monthly check in the site repository, .github/workflows/settings-check.yml , runs --check for every listed repository with a fine-grained personal access token on those repositories, expiring yearly, stored as the secret SETTINGS_READ_TOKEN . The token holds read access, and nothing more, for: Administration (the Actions permissions), Metadata (the rulesets), Actions (the environments and their deployment branch policies), Environments (the environment secrets), Secrets and Variables (the repository's own); a permission missing from the token reads as permanent drift, because unreadable counts as drift. On drift it opens one issue in the site repository, or updates the open one, with the full report. It never applies anything, and no write-capable administration token ever exists in CI. The monthly workflow is committed with manual dispatch only. Once the token exists, the owner creates the secret and adds the schedule block that the file's comment shows; nothing else changes. When the token expires, the check fails loudly at its first step rather than passing silently. Owner steps when adopting the standard Merge the repository's scaffold PR, so that validate.yml and the Validate targets check exist before the ruleset requires them. Run python3 tools/repo_settings.py --repo owner/game --apply and --repo owner/game-build --apply from a site repository checkout. Do the printed hand steps: create the DATA_APP_CLIENT_ID variable and the DATA_APP_PRIVATE_KEY environment secret, delete the credentials and variables of any earlier process, confirm the package grant, and remove from the ruleset any required check whose job no longer exists. Once, for the site repository: create the read-only token and the SETTINGS_READ_TOKEN secret, then enable the monthly schedule. A repository that still holds the key as a repository secret moves it in this order. A job that references an environment reads the environment's secret when it has one of that name and otherwise falls back to the repository secret, so while both exist a published line proves nothing about the environment secret; the order below deletes the repository secret first and then demands a publish. Create the publish environment with its branch policy and the environment secret, and the empty validate environment ( Publishing ); --apply creates both environments and the policy, the secret is by hand. Merge the validate.yml change that references the environments (the kit sync). Delete the repository secret DATA_APP_PRIVATE_KEY (Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions, Secrets). Run the workflow on main by hand (Actions, Validate, Run workflow, branch main ) and require Publish to the site to print published ... . A failure at Mint a data-repository token means the environment secret is wrong: fix it and run again; nothing was published in between, and the next run publishes. Prove the branch policy, with both probes; they are the only evidence that it applies with deployment: false : GitHub's text on deployment: false says that wait timers and required reviewers still apply and does not list deployment branch policies among the rules that apply. On a throwaway branch change the environment line to name: publish , then (a) open a draft pull request: every Validate <target id> job must be refused before its first step with an environment protection message; (b) run the workflow by hand on that branch (Actions, Validate, Run workflow, choose the branch): refused the same way. Close the pull request and delete the branch. A probe that runs instead of being refused means the key is reachable from branches: delete the environment secret at once and report it. python3 tools/repo_settings.py --repo owner/game --check reports no drift. Assumptions to confirm The actions-allowlist, retention and fork-approval endpoints behave as documented for personal accounts. Manage Actions access is still the package-level grant that lets the source repository pull the image. Every agent authors under the owner's login. That is what makes a native approval rule pointless and the procedural merge authority of Contribution workflow the right shape. If agents ever get their own accounts, add one required approving review from the owner with stale approvals dismissed, and nothing else changes.

title: Data contract
summary: The schema-1 files the publish action writes and the checker that enforces them.
text: Data contract The schema-1 files the publish action writes and the checker that enforces them. The authoritative text is contract/README.md in the site repository, and its executable form is publish.py check <tree> : if the two ever disagree, the checker is right. A copy of the contract is in the starter archive. This chapter restates it for the producer's point of view. Layout index.json {"schema": 1, "games": ["game", ...]} data/game/game.json presentation and the target list data/game/cover.webp optional, committed by hand data/game/cover-thumb.webp generated on deploy: 360px wide, what the site displays data/game/GAME01-rev0/latest.json the newest measurement data/game/GAME01-rev0/history.json every measurement, append-only data/game/GAME01-rev0/map.json the newest measurement's tile map data/game/GAME01-rev0/contributors.json optional A (game, target) pair is the unit of everything; a game with one target has one entry. Only active targets have a directory. The producer owns config/targets.json and config/site.json ( Targets ); the action derives everything else from them and from the objdiff report. game.json site.json plus repository ( owner/game ), defaultTarget and targets from targets.json , with schema: 1 . Rewritten by every publish of any active target. latest.json {"schema": 1, "game": "game", "target": "GAME01-rev0", "source": {"revision": "<commit sha>", "committedAt": "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z", "title": "<commit subject>", "url": "https://github.com/owner/game/commit/<sha>", "runUrl": "https://github.com/owner/game/actions/runs/<id>"}, "measuredAt": "2026-01-02T00:01:00Z", "tools": [{"name": "build-environment", "version": "ghcr.io/owner/game-build@sha256:..."}, {"name": "dtk", "version": "v1.8.3"}, {"name": "objdiff", "version": "v3.6.1"}], "summary": { "code": {"total": 1618968, "linked": 213044, "matched": 260640, "fuzzy": 292438.68}, "data": {"total": 870056, "linked": 131316, "matched": 157536, "fuzzy": 183267.63}, "functions": {"total": 4746, "exact": 1253, "named": 2595}, "files": {"total": 519, "exact": 119, "named": 374}}, "modules": {"map": "map.json", "contributors": null}, "digests": {"map.json": "3f0c6a9e5b1d2c47", "history.json": "9a71e0c4d2b8f615"}} Field Meaning source The measured commit: its SHA, commit time, subject, URL and the CI run that measured it ( runUrl is the provenance) digests For each of map.json , history.json and contributors.json beside this file: the first 16 hex digits of its SHA-256. The page fetches those files by digest ( ?v=<digest> ), so a corrected file is a new URL ( Publishing , "Correcting published data"). Absent in data published before the digests existed; the page then keys by the revision measuredAt The measured-at input, UTC tools The tools input, one object per line summary.code , summary.data Bytes of the original: total , linked (units that link into the byte-identical executable), matched (bytes matching exactly, linked or not), fuzzy (size-weighted similarity; may be null ) summary.functions total , exact (100% match) and named (symbol is not fn_<hex> or func_<hex> ); may be null summary.files Units: total , named (not tool-generated) and exact (named and fully matched); may be null modules map names the map file; contributors names the optional contributors file or is null linked , matched and fuzzy overlap and are never added together. matched <= fuzzy <= total , exactly: there is no tolerance, in the checker or on the page, so a fuzzy value a rounding step below matched is refused, which is why the action holds a data section's fuzzy within those bounds when it converts a percentage back into bytes. history.json A JSON array, one row per line, ordered by measuredAt , at most one row per revision: [ {"code":{"total":1610980,"linked":0,"matched":null,"fuzzy":null},"data":{"total":870068,"linked":0,"matched":null,"fuzzy":null},"functions":null,"measuredAt":"2026-10-26T16:34:26Z","revision":"<sha>","legacy":{"provenance":{"kind":"measured","source":"validate.yml run 40360367860"}}}, {"code":{"total":1618968,"linked":213044,"matched":260640,"fuzzy":292438.68},"data":{"total":870056,"linked":131316,"matched":157536,"fuzzy":183267.63},"functions":{"total":4746,"exact":1253,"named":2595},"measuredAt":"2026-10-27T19:52:22Z","revision":"<sha>"} ] Each row carries revision , measuredAt , code , data and functions from the measurement. The action appends one row per newly measured revision and never edits or removes a row. Rows imported from an older system keep whatever they had (missing measures are null ) and their original provenance under legacy ; nothing writes legacy today. The latest revision's row equals latest.json 's total and linked . The site draws the history chart from this file, so the first main publish starts the chart with one point; there is no way, and no need, to backfill. map.json {"schema": 1, "files": [<node>, ...], "sections": [<node>, ...]} : two views of the same bytes. files groups function tiles by source unit (what the page draws) and adds one data tile per unit; sections groups the same functions by code section plus one Data sections group. A node is {"name", "kind": "code"|"data", "size", "linked", "matched", "fuzzy"} plus either address (a leaf) or mapped_extents ( [{"start", "end"}] , hex), and optionally children . Function leaves add "type": "function" , function_address and original_size . Code a unit's functions do not cover (alignment padding, code the producer does not split into functions) is one leaf per section piece named <unit> (other code) , without a type , holding the matched bytes no exact function accounts for; dtk-template reports have none. The checker enforces that a parent's measures are its children's sums, that extents never overlap, that both views cover exactly the same bytes, that per kind the top-level nodes sum to the summary, and that every function is covered once with counts matching the summary. The action builds the map from the same report as the summary, so a producer never writes it by hand. contributors.json Optional; modules.contributors names it when present. The publish action writes it when the producer's config/site.json sets "contributors": true ( Publishing , "Credits"); otherwise it writes "contributors": null . The shape is {"schema": 1, "credited_functions": N, "contributors": [{"id", "login", "functions"}], "functions": [{"id": "<target>:<address>:<size>", "authors": [id], "since"}], "retired": [...], "people": [{"id", "login"}]} . Every exact function is credited once and the totals agree with the summary; contributors is the ranking (everyone with a credit, most functions first, then by login); since is the commit time of the earliest measured build in which the function was exact (a credit imported without one is kept as it is); retired keeps the credits of functions no longer exact, never overlapping the current ones; people names everyone a credit refers to. The page shows contributor rankings only when the file exists. Validation rules the producer meets Rule Where it bites Target ids [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ , unique; default listed; platform lower case; sha1 40 lower-case hex; status in active , planned , archived targets.json slug [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]* ; title and console non-empty strings site.json Report function count and exact count equal its measures The objdiff report; a mismatch means a different objdiff version or an edited report Every function inside a code section of its unit; data sections sum to the unit's total_data The report against code-sections Timestamps UTC ISO 8601 measured-at One history row per revision, in measuredAt order Only the action writes it Every digest in latest.json equals its file's A hand correction without publish.py reseal Versioning Adding a field never changes schema ; readers ignore fields they do not know. A breaking change bumps schema , rewrites the whole data repository in one commit and switches the site in the same change; the action at @main follows, and producers pick it up on their next run without editing anything. Writers are strict and readers are lenient: the action refuses anything the checker rejects, and the site shows "unavailable" for a target whose files do not parse. Two readers check the data: publish.py check before every push, and the page's own validator before every draw. They must agree, and the site repository keeps them agreeing in two ways: its tests run the page's validator on what the publisher writes, and its Live data job runs python3 tools/check_data_tree.py on a fresh clone of the data repository, with both readers, on every change to the site and once a day. The job checks every target that has a measurement, archived ones included, which is more than the page shows and exactly what every publish enforces. It is its own job, which the deploy does not wait for: a bad publish in another repository must not block the site, and a red run names the game, target, file and the data repository's commit. If the data is wrong, correct it ( Publishing ); if the new check is wrong, fix the check.

title: The site
summary: How the data repository is served and read, cover art, URLs and local preview.
text: The site How the data repository is served and read, cover art, URLs and local preview. The site is static. It builds nothing and imports nothing: mitsevox/mitsevox.github.io deploys its own HTML, scripts and this wiki to GitHub Pages, and at view time the page fetches /decomp-data/ from the same origin, which is the data repository's Pages deployment. A producer therefore never needs a pull request against the site. The one thing committed to the data repository by hand is cover art. The data repository's deploy mitsevox/decomp-data holds index.json , .nojekyll , data/ and one workflow, deploy.yml . Every publish is a push to main , and a push made with a GitHub App token starts the workflow, which checks out main and deploys the whole repository to Pages with actions/upload-pages-artifact and actions/deploy-pages . Its concurrency group is pages with cancel-in-progress: false : one deploy runs, one waits, and a burst of publishes collapses into a couple of deploys that each publish the branch tip. Pages serves it at https://mitsevox.github.io/decomp-data/ . For a new data repository of your own: create it public, add index.json with {"schema": 1, "games": []} , an empty .nojekyll and the same deploy.yml , and set the repository's Pages source to GitHub Actions ( documentation ). The site repository's frontend reads /decomp-data/ on its own origin, so a separate site would be a fork of the site repository with that path changed; that is outside this guide. How a page is composed For /games/game/?target=GAME01-rev0 the page reads: index.json , to know the games. data/game/game.json : title, console, year, repository link, contributions , artwork , defaultTarget and the target list. The target picker appears when there is more than one target and groups them by label , then revision . data/game/GAME01-rev0/latest.json for each active target: the summary bars (linked, matched and fuzzy for code and data), the function and file counts when they are not null , the measured commit and run links, and the tools list. data/game/GAME01-rev0/map.json when the summary's modules.map names it: the tile map. data/game/GAME01-rev0/history.json : the progress chart. data/game/GAME01-rev0/contributors.json when modules.contributors names it: rankings. latest.json is revalidated on every view; map.json , history.json and contributors.json are fetched by the digest latest.json gives them ( ?v=<digest> ) and cached as immutable, so a corrected file reaches a browser at its next load after the deploy (Pages' edge cache holds a file for about ten minutes; a tab that stays open keeps the latest.json it loaded) ( Publishing , "Correcting published data"). Without ?target= , the page shows defaultTarget . A target that is not active is listed without a measurement. A target whose latest.json fails to load shows "unavailable" and leaves the rest of the game alone; a map or history file that fails the page's checks hides only its own section. The hub at / lists every game in index.json with its default target's code and data bars, the cover, the console icon chosen from console , and the latest commit. Cover art Covers are committed by hand to the data repository, not published by CI, so that rights-sensitive images never pass through the producer or the automation: Prepare cover.webp at the original aspect ratio (the reference covers are 1112 by 1600 pixels). Commit it as data/<slug>/cover.webp in the data repository. The directory exists after the first publish; committing the cover earlier is fine too, since the publish only writes its own files. Add "artwork": {"cover": "cover.webp", "width": 1112, "height": 1600} to the producer's config/site.json and merge. The next publish carries it into game.json . Until both halves are in place the page shows no cover; an artwork entry without the file is a broken image. URLs URL Serves https://mitsevox.github.io/ The hub https://mitsevox.github.io/games/<slug>/ The game at its default target https://mitsevox.github.io/games/<slug>/?target=<id> The game at one target https://mitsevox.github.io/decomp-data/data/<slug>/<id>/latest.json The raw data, same for every file in the data repository https://mitsevox.github.io/wiki/ This guide The site repository's deploy stages one games/<slug>/index.html for every slug in the live index.json , so an established game's page answers with status 200. A game added since the last site deploy renders through the 404.html shell, which is the same application; it becomes a real file at the next site deploy, which the owner can trigger with workflow_dispatch on the site's Site workflow. Previewing locally Clone the site repository and the data repository, then serve the site at / and the data checkout at /decomp-data/ with 404.html as the fallback for unknown paths. The dry-run tree from Publishing can stand in for the data checkout to preview a game before its first real publish. The site repository's README has the same instructions and the test command ( python3 -m unittest discover -s tests ). What never needs a site change Adding a game, adding a target, renaming a title, changing the cover, accepting contributions: all of these are edits to config/site.json , config/targets.json or the data repository. The site changes only when the contract changes or the presentation does.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Failure messages from the build, the publish action and the page, with their causes.
text: Troubleshooting Failure messages from the build, the publish action and the page, with their causes. Find the layer that failed before changing anything: the plan, the tool tests, the image pull, the original, the build, the report conversion, the push, the deploy or the page. Each layer has its own messages, listed below as they appear in the job log. Plan and tool tests Message Cause and fix Invalid target registry , Unknown target fields , Invalid target identity , Invalid target status , Duplicate target config/targets.json breaks a rule in Targets : exactly the seven fields per target, lower-case platform, 40 lower-case hex digits, status in active , planned , archived . Default target is not active defaultTarget names a planned or archived target. Invalid CI dependency map , Unsafe CI dependency patterns config/ci-targets.json : exactly the keys schemaVersion , shared and nonBuild , no leading / or .. in patterns. Target defines collide Two ids in targets.json give the same VERSION_ define ( a-b and a.b , say); rename one. Diff endpoints must be full commit SHAs The planner ran outside Actions or with an unusual event; run it with --force-all to audit everything. config/<id>/build.sha1 differs from targets.json , config/<id>/config.yml hash differs from targets.json , config/<id>/<file> is missing tools/targets.py check : the three hashes of a target disagree, or an active target lacks a file. Fix the odd one out; the original's hash is the truth. unknown VERSION_ token , version condition mixed with other macros , BUILD_VERSION is never read in source , MatchingFor argument ... is not a known target id , #else after a version condition: it covers every target not named , a version condition that holds for every target not named tools/versions.py check : see the Version differences section of Build, verify, measure . The last two are warnings while two targets are listed and errors from the third; view and diff still resolve the branch. new_target: refusing to overwrite config/<id>/... The target's directory holds a file that is neither the tool's own stub nor a lone placeholder README.md : real content. Move it aside or scaffold by hand ( Targets ). matching_scope: pin names ...; the active targets are ... , matching_scope: Object calls whose first argument is not ... , matching_scope: Matching is used outside Object(Matching, ...) pin must name every active target, all of them, with the new target still planned or archived ; an Object call with an alias or a literal as its first argument, or a use of Matching as a value ( flag = Matching ), is pinned by hand before the tool runs. evidence.tsv:<line>: ... tools/evidence.py check : the row breaks the format in config/README.md (columns, address form, kind, origin, edges). ::warning file=...:: lines in Check the scaffold The checkout drifts from the kit or the spec ( Starter kit ). Warnings do not fail the job until the owner sets strict: true . Image and original Message Cause and fix The job fails while initializing the container (pull denied, unauthorized, manifest unknown) The package is not readable by the public repository, or the digest is wrong. In the private package's settings add owner/game under Manage Actions access with Read, and copy the digest from the image workflow's summary. cp: cannot stat '/orig/<id>/sys/main.dol' The image does not hold that target, or the path differs from PARAMETER 2. Add the COPY and checksum to the Dockerfile and rebuild, or fix the path in both places. The toolkit reports a hash mismatch when splitting The file at orig/<id>/<path> is not the binary config.yml names. Fix the file or, if the file is right, the hash in config.yml , build.sha1 and targets.json together (then the image's checksum line too). sha1sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match during docker build The original committed to the private repository differs from the Dockerfile's checksum line. Build and measurement Symptom Cause and fix configure.py rejects --version The id is not an active target in config/targets.json , or configure.py was not wired to tools/targets.py ( Build, verify, measure ). The link succeeds but the hash check against config/<id>/build.sha1 fails A Matching object no longer matches, or build.sha1 is wrong. Mark the object NonMatching until it matches; build.sha1 must equal the original's sha1 . ninja: error: ... report.json or no report written The progress / report.json targets need objdiff; check config.objdiff_tag and network access from the image, or pass --objdiff to a local binary. Numbers look wrong on the page but the build is green Compare with a local measurement at the same commit ( ninja ... progress with dtk-template). linked only counts Matching units; matched counts exact functions anywhere; fuzzy is size-weighted. A new split or a renamed unit changes files counts without changing bytes. measuring_tools: BUILD_IMAGE is not a digest-pinned image reference The BUILD_IMAGE variable in validate.yml is not of the form ghcr.io/<name>@sha256:<64 hex> , or the tool was run outside the workflow without it in the environment. measuring_tools: configure.py has no objdiff_tag The config.<tag> = "<version>" line is missing or formatted differently; edit TAGS in tools/measuring_tools.py or the line. measuring_tools: dtk reports 'dtk 1.8.4'; the repository pins v1.8.3 The image's tool and the repository's pin disagree: an image digest bumped without the pin, or the pin without the image. Change the one that is wrong, deliberately ( Build environment ); never publish a provenance the image does not match. measuring_tools: cannot run dtk --version to verify dtk VERIFY in tools/measuring_tools.py names a command the image does not have at that path; fix the command or the image. Publish step Every message from publish.py is prefixed publish: and fails the step; nothing is pushed. The Check the report step of a pull request prints the same messages for the report and contract causes, so a report problem is found before main ; the history and credits messages cannot occur there, because the check writes into an empty tree without credits. Message Cause and fix The Mint a data-repository token step fails The App is not installed on the data repository, the client id or private key is wrong or empty, or the App lacks Contents read and write. Check the variable name and the publish environment's secret name in validate.yml against the repository settings. The environment's secret wins when the environment has one of that name; a job whose environment lacks it falls back to a repository secret of that name, which is why the move order deletes the repository secret before trusting a publish ( Repository settings ). A Validate <target id> job of a branch is refused before its first step with an environment protection message The run referenced the publish environment outside main : that branch's validate.yml changed the environment line. Restore the kit's line ( CI ). DATA_TOKEN is not set The script ran outside the action without the token; use --dry-run locally. --repository or GITHUB_REPOSITORY is required Local run: pass --repository owner/game . Target <id> is not an active target of <slug> The published target is planned or archived in targets.json . targets.json lists no targets , Duplicate target id , Default target is not listed , Invalid target id , <id>: platform must be a lower-case name , <id>: sha1 must be 40 lower-case hex digits , <id>: status must be active, planned or archived config/targets.json ; tools/targets.py would have rejected these too, so the tool tests catch them first. site.json: invalid slug , site.json: title is required , site.json: console is required config/site.json . Report lists N functions, its measures say M , Report has N exact functions, its measures say M The report's own totals disagree with its function list: an objdiff version with different semantics, or an edited report. Pin config.objdiff_tag to a known-good version. <unit>: <function> lies outside the code sections .init, .text The platform's code sections are named differently; pass code-sections to the action. <unit>: data sections do not add up to total_data A unit's total_data disagrees with its section sizes; usually the same objdiff version problem. history: duplicate revision , history: rows out of order , <slug>/<id>: history lacks the latest revision The data repository's existing files are inconsistent; someone edited them by hand. Revert that commit in the data repository. map.json: digest differs from latest.json; run publish.py reseal A file was corrected by hand without the reseal step ( Publishing , "Correcting published data"). Reseal and check in a data-repository pull request. push failed (attempt N), retrying then push failed after 5 attempts Five consecutive lost races or a rejected push. Re-run the job; if it persists, check the App's permission and branch rules on the data repository. <slug>/<id> <sha> already published Not an error: the revision was published before (a re-run). The first measurement of a revision wins. Deploy and page Symptom Cause and fix The data repository has the commit but the page is old The data repository's Deploy workflow takes about a minute and queues bursts; wait, then reload. If Deploy did not run, the Pages source is not set to GitHub Actions. A target shows "unavailable" Its latest.json does not load or parse. A map.json or history.json that fails the page's checks hides only its own section ("Progress history unavailable"). Run python3 tools/check_data_tree.py from the site repository on a clone of the data repository to find the file with both readers. The page shows a map that was corrected in the data repository as it was before The correction was committed without publish.py reseal , so its URL did not change and browsers keep the cached copy. Reseal ( Publishing ); the page refetches on its own only when the cached copy fails validation. The game is missing from the hub Its slug is not in index.json ; the first publish adds it. Check that the publish step ran on main (the condition is github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') ). /games/<slug>/ returns 404 with the application shell Normal for a game added since the last site deploy; the page still renders. The next site deploy stages a real file. No cover Both halves are needed: data/<slug>/cover.webp in the data repository and artwork in config/site.json followed by a publish. No Contribute link contributions.accepting is false , or there is no guideUrl , or the target has no report. The history chart has one point Expected after the first publish; every later main publish adds one. The site repository's Live data job fails A change to the site made a reader stricter than something already published, or the data repository holds a hand edit the checkers refuse, or the daily run found a bad publish. The log names the game, target and file, and the data repository's commit it checked. If the data is wrong, correct it ( Publishing ); if the new check is wrong, fix the check. The deploy does not wait for this job. Settings Symptom Cause and fix repo_settings.py --check reports found unreadable The token lacks Administration: read for that setting, or the endpoint does not exist on this plan (rulesets on a private repository, say). Unreadable counts as drift on purpose. The monthly check fails at Require the read-only token The SETTINGS_READ_TOKEN secret is missing or expired; create a new yearly token ( Repository settings ). Check the scaffold warns settings: ... The repository's description, topics, features, merge settings or main rules differ from the standard; run --apply with the owner's token. repo_settings.py --check reports environments.publish.branches: expected ["main"] or actions.secrets: expected [] The publish environment allows every branch, or the key is still a repository secret. --apply sets the branch policy; the secret moves by hand ( Repository settings , the move order). Recovery A bad publish is a git revert in the data repository followed by publish.py reseal ; the next publish appends on top. A wrong published file is corrected the same way, by a resealed data-repository pull request ( Publishing , "Correcting published data"), never by re-running the measurement, which keeps what was published first. A bad image digest is a revert of the validate.yml change. Never loosen a check, change a count or alter the build image to make a contribution pass; report the problem in an issue for the owner.

text: Starter kit The downloadable files, their parameters, the scaffold spec, the acceptance checklist and an agent prompt. Download the repository starter archive . Class Files Checked Byte-identical tools/targets.py , tools/ci_targets.py , tools/versions.py , tools/evidence.py , tools/new_target.py , tools/matching_scope.py , tools/tier.py , tools/credits.py , tests/test_targets.py , config/README.md Equal to the kit at the action's revision Outline README.md (the seven headings in order), CONTRIBUTING.md (the section headings), AGENTS.md (the kit header verbatim, then ## Project ), .github/pull_request_template.md (contains ## Targets ), validate.yml (job names, step names, the publish, report-check and scaffold-check actions, BUILD_IMAGE by digest, the target job's environment line) Headings or the fixed part; the body is free Free Everything else Nothing The other checks: every required path present, a build entry point present, the root allowlist, the per-target files for each status, the three hashes agreeing per target, every MatchingFor argument and VERSION_ token known, ci-targets.json without a targets key, evidence.tsv well formed, no docs/dtk/ or config.example.yml , no file in references/ over 4 MB, .gitignore covering orig/*/* , build/ , *.dol and *.elf , no second workflow, and the readable half of the settings standard . There is no exception file: a process that needs one is a process the allowlist was wrong about, and project material goes under docs/ , tools/ or references/ . Acceptance checklist The repository is set up when each line is true and can be shown with a run, a commit or a URL. The public repository has the layout in Repository layout ; git status after a local build shows no original or generated file. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' , python3 tools/targets.py check , python3 tools/versions.py check and python3 tools/evidence.py check pass locally. ninja -f build/<id>/build.ninja produces the byte-identical executable for every active target. The measurement command of the README writes build/<id>/report.json , and publish.py publish --dry-run --no-credits converts it ( Publishing ). The private repository's image workflow is green on main , the package is private, the public repository has Read access, and validate.yml names the digest in BUILD_IMAGE . A pull request runs Plan affected targets , Tool tests , Validate <id> and Validate targets , all green, and the Check the scaffold step prints no warning. The main ruleset requires a pull request and Validate targets , and the merges ruleset restricts merging to the Repository admin role; python3 tools/repo_settings.py --repo owner/game --check reports no drift for either repository. The GitHub App is installed on the data repository; the producer holds the variable and the publish environment with the secret. The first main run's Publish to the site step printed published <slug>/<id> <sha> ; the data repository has the commit; https://mitsevox.github.io/games/<slug>/ shows it.
